summary: Iteration 14: Tested /api/ai/picks 'Picked for you by Buddy' dashboard row end-to-end. Wrote 10 pytest cases (backend/tests/test_iteration14_ai_picks.py) — all pass. Verified auth (401 without token), shape (1-3 picks with why lines), geography sanity (India members get India cities only), joined-event exclusion, per-member isolation (Diya vs Tara), cache semantics (same generated_at on second call), refresh?=1 regenerates, hydration guard drops draft/past events (verified by flipping a picked event to draft and confirming it disappears from the reused cache while others remain, then restored), unique index on ai_picks.user_id. Frontend playwright: logged in as diya.sharma, ai-picks-section renders with 3 cards + 3 why lines with natural copy (e.g., 'You like sports, and Pune keeps this football pickup in India at a low INR 300.'), no forbidden prompt words, ai-picks-refresh triggers loading skeleton then new cards, first event link /events/<id> returns 200, no horizontal overflow at 1920px or 390px, dash-tile-*, dash-referral-card, quick-ai still render.
critical_code_review_comments: ai_hydrate_picks compares starts_at (datetime) with iso(now_utc()) (ISO string). This works because events are stored with ISO string starts_at and lexicographic compare matches chronological for ISO-8601 UTC, but it is fragile — recommend using a real datetime comparison to future-proof against timezone or format drift.

GET /api/ai/picks with refresh=1 makes an LLM call every time; consider a lightweight per-user rate limit (e.g. 1 refresh per minute) to protect the shared Emergent LLM balance from a user hammering the Refresh button.

When the LLM returns no valid picks after refresh, endpoint returns empty items without updating the cache — subsequent refresh will call the LLM again. Consider caching an empty result briefly to avoid runaway billing on a broken prompt.
seed_data_creation: None. Draft-flip test restores original status in finally block.
